title: Anar al metge / Going to the doctor
bridge: In Catalan, when talking about going to the doctor, the verb 'anar' (to go) is commonly used, similar to English. However, Catalan often uses the preposition 'al' (to the) before 'metge' (doctor), which is a contraction of 'a' (to) and 'el' (the). Be careful not to directly translate 'going to the doctor' as 'anar al doctor' in Catalan, as 'metge' is the correct term. Additionally, Catalan speakers often use the phrase 'tinc una visita' (I have an appointment) instead of just saying 'appointment'.
rule: To express going to the doctor in Catalan, use the structure 'Anar al metge'. For appointments, say 'Tinc una visita mèdica'. When describing symptoms, use the verb 'tindre' (to have) followed by the symptom, e.g., 'Tinc mal de cap' (I have a headache). Remember that Catalan adjectives often come after the noun, unlike in English. For example, 'dolor fort' (strong pain) instead of 'fort dolor'.

title: Reservar un hotel / Booking a hotel
bridge: In Catalan, when booking accommodation, the verb 'reservar' is used similarly to English, but the structure of the sentence often places the object pronoun before the verb, which is different from English. Additionally, Catalan uses formal and informal forms of address ('vostè' and 'tu'), which can affect verb conjugations and politeness. Be cautious with false friends like 'habitació' (room) and 'pis' (floor/apartment), as 'pis' in Catalan does not mean 'floor' in the sense of a level in a building.
rule: To book accommodation in Catalan, use the verb 'reservar' followed by the object. For example, 'Vull reservar una habitació' (I want to book a room). When asking about availability, use 'Hi ha' (There is/are) or 'Teniu' (Do you have). Remember to use 'per' for 'for' when specifying duration, e.g., 'per tres nits' (for three nights). Formal and informal forms of address affect verb conjugations: 'vostè' (formal) uses the third person, while 'tu' (informal) uses the second person.

title: Canviar diners / Exchanging Money
bridge: In Catalan, when exchanging money, you'll often use the verb 'canviar' (to exchange), which is similar to English. However, be careful with false friends like 'cambio' (which means 'change' in Spanish but is not used the same way in Catalan). Also, Catalan uses the preposition 'per' to indicate the currency you want to exchange into, unlike English which uses 'to' or 'into'.
rule: To talk about exchanging money in Catalan, use the structure: 'Vull canviar [amount] [currency] per [currency]'. For example, 'Vull canviar 100 dòlars per euros'. Note that 'dòlars' and 'euros' are plural forms in Catalan. Always use the verb 'canviar' in the first person singular ('vull canviar') for polite requests.

title: Presentació personal / Personal Introduction
bridge: In Catalan, introducing yourself in a job interview involves a more formal tone than in English. While English speakers often use 'Hi' or 'Hello,' Catalan speakers typically use 'Bon dia' or 'Bona tarda' depending on the time of day. Additionally, Catalan speakers often include their full name and a brief description of their background, which is more detailed than the usual English introduction.
rule: When introducing yourself in Catalan, start with a greeting appropriate to the time of day ('Bon dia' for morning, 'Bona tarda' for afternoon/evening). Follow with your full name and a concise description of your professional background. Use the formal 'vostè' form when addressing the interviewer, unless invited to use 'tu'.

title: Enviar un paquet / Sending a Package
bridge: In Catalan, when sending a package at the post office, you'll notice that the vocabulary is quite similar to English, but the sentence structure and verb usage can differ. For instance, 'enviar' (to send) is used more frequently than in English, where 'send' might be replaced by 'post' or 'mail'. Additionally, Catalan often uses the preposition 'a' (to) before the recipient, which is not always necessary in English.
rule: To express sending a package in Catalan, use the verb 'enviar' followed by the preposition 'a' and the recipient. For example, 'Envio un paquet a Barcelona' (I send a package to Barcelona). The verb 'enviar' is regular in the present tense: jo envio, tu envies, ell/ella/vostè envia, nosaltres enviem, vosaltres envieu, ells/elles/vostès envien. Remember to use the correct article before the noun, such as 'un paquet' (a package) or 'el paquet' (the package).

title: Alquilar un pis / Renting a Flat
bridge: In Catalan, when renting a flat, you'll notice that the vocabulary for housing and rental terms is quite different from English. For instance, 'pis' means 'flat' and 'alquilar' means 'to rent'. Be careful with false friends like 'lloguer' (rent) which sounds like 'log' but means 'rental'. Additionally, Catalan uses formal and informal registers more distinctly than English, so it's important to use 'vostè' (formal you) when speaking to landlords or agents.
rule: When discussing renting a flat in Catalan, use the verb 'alquilar' for 'to rent'. The present tense is 'alquilo' (I rent), 'alquiles' (you rent), 'alquila' (he/she rents), 'alquilem' (we rent), 'alquileu' (you all rent), and 'alquilen' (they rent). For the future, use 'alquilaré' (I will rent), 'alquilaràs' (you will rent), etc. Remember to use the formal 'vostè' form when addressing strangers or professionals. Key phrases include 'Estic buscant un pis per llogar' (I'm looking for a flat to rent) and 'Quan està disponible?' (When is it available?)

title: Salutacions i presentacions / Greetings and introductions
bridge: In Catalan, greetings and introductions are more formal than in English, especially with strangers or older people. The word 'Hola' is used for hello, similar to English, but 'Adéu' for goodbye is less common in informal settings, where 'Fin' or 'Fins aviat' are preferred. Be careful with the word order in introductions, as the verb 'ser' (to be) is often omitted in Catalan, unlike in English.
rule: When greeting someone in Catalan, use 'Hola' followed by the person's name or a title (e.g., Senyor, Senyora). For introductions, the structure is 'Em dic [name]' (My name is [name]) or ' Sóc [name]' (I am [name]). The verb 'ser' is often omitted in informal introductions. Remember to use the correct title (Senyor/Senyora) when addressing someone you don't know well. In informal settings, 'Ei' or 'Ei, què tal?' can be used as a casual greeting.

title: Quejar-se i demanar disculpes / Complaining and Apologizing
bridge: In Catalan, complaining and apologizing often involve more formal expressions than in English, especially in polite contexts. Unlike English, where 'I'm sorry' is versatile, Catalan distinguishes between apologies and excuses more clearly. Be cautious with false friends like 'sorry' and 'disculpa', as their usage differs slightly.
rule: To complain, use phrases like 'Em sap greu dir-ho, però...' (I’m sorry to say, but...) or 'Tinc una queixa sobre...' (I have a complaint about...). For apologies, 'De debò, ho sento' (I really apologize) or 'Disculpa les molèsties' (Sorry for the inconvenience) are common. Note that 'ho sento' is more formal than 'disculpa'. Always use the formal 'vostè' form when addressing strangers or in formal settings.

concept_examples.text: De debò, ho sento per l’error.

concept_examples.phonetic: /də dəˈβo u ˈsɛnto pər ləˈɾoɾ/

concept_examples.text: Disculpa, no era la meva intenció.
concept_examples.translation: Sorry, it wasn’t my intention.
concept_examples.phonetic: /disˈkulpə ˈno ˈeɾa la ˈmɛva inˈtenˈsjo/

concept_examples.text: Tinc una queixa sobre el producte.
concept_examples.translation: I have a complaint about the product.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ˈtin una ˈkɛtʃa ˈsoβɾə əl pɾoˈdute/

common_error.explanation: English speakers often directly translate 'sorry' to 'sorry' in Catalan, but 'sorry' is not commonly used in Catalan. Instead, use 'ho sento' or 'disculpa' depending on the formality of the situation.

examples.note: Use simple sentences to express dissatisfaction.
Add adverbs like 'molt' to emphasize the complaint.
Use 'ho sento' for sincere apologies.
Use 'disculpa' for lighter apologies or excuses.

examples.original: Em sap greu dir-ho, però el producte està defectuós.
examples.phonetic: /əm ˈsap ˈɣɾew ˈdiɾu ˈpeɾo əl pɾoˈdukte əˈsta dəfəkˈtuos/
examples.translation: I’m sorry to say it, but the product is defective.
examples.note: Combine polite expressions with complaints.

examples.original: De debò, ho sento per la confusió.
examples.phonetic: /də dəˈβo u ˈsɛnto pər la kuŋfuˈzio/
examples.translation: I really apologize for the confusion.
examples.note: Use 'de debò' to emphasize sincerity in apologies.

title: Descriure la teva ciutat o poble / Describing Your Hometown
bridge: In Catalan, describing your hometown involves using specific adjectives and structures that may differ from English. For instance, Catalan often uses the verb 'ser' (to be) for permanent characteristics, similar to English, but the adjective placement can vary. Be cautious with false friends like 'car' (expensive) vs. English 'car'. Additionally, Catalan uses the preposition 'a' to indicate location, unlike English's 'in' or 'at'.
rule: To describe your hometown in Catalan, use the structure 'La meva ciutat/poble és...'. Adjectives generally follow the noun, but some common adjectives like 'gran' (big) or 'petita' (small) can precede it for emphasis. Use 'hi ha' (there is/are) to mention places or features. For location, use 'a' + city/town name. Remember, Catalan adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.

concept_examples.text: La meva ciutat és gran i té molts parcs.
concept_examples.translation: My city is big and has many parks.
concept_examples.phonetic: /lə ˈmeβə siˈutat ˈes ˈɣɾan i ˈte ˈmɔlts ˈpaɾks/

concept_examples.text: El meu poble és petit però molt acollidor.
concept_examples.translation: My town is small but very welcoming.
concept_examples.phonetic: /əl ˈməu ˈpɔβlə ˈes pəˈˈtɾiɾ pəˈˈɾo ˈmɔɫt əkuˈʎiðoɾ/

concept_examples.text: Hi ha un riu a prop de la meva ciutat.
concept_examples.translation: There is a river near my city.
concept_examples.phonetic: /hi ˈa ˈuŋ ˈriw ə ˈpɾɔp də lə ˈmeβə siˈutat/

concept_examples.text: A Barcelona hi ha molts museus interessants.
concept_examples.translation: In Barcelona, there are many interesting museums.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ə βəɾsəˈɫonə hi ˈa ˈmɔlts muˈzeus intəɾəˈsants/

common_error.wrong: My city is very car and have many parks.
common_error.correct: La meva ciutat és molt cara i té molts parcs.
common_error.correct_alt: La meva ciutat és molt gran i té molts parcs.
common_error.explanation: English speakers often confuse 'car' (expensive) with the English word 'car'. Additionally, 'have' in English translates to 'té' (has) in Catalan, not 'have'. The correct adjective for 'big' is 'gran', not 'car'.

examples.note: Use 'gran' to describe size, e.g., 'La meva ciutat és gran'.
Use 'petit' for smaller places, e.g., 'El meu poble és petit'.
Describes a friendly atmosphere, e.g., 'és molt acollidor'.
Use 'parc' to describe green spaces, e.g., 'Hi ha molts parcs'.
Describes a natural feature, e.g., 'Hi ha un riu a prop'.
Use 'museu' for cultural places, e.g., 'Hi ha molts museus'.
Use 'a prop de' to indicate proximity, e.g., 'a prop de la ciutat'.
Use 'a' for location, e.g., 'A Barcelona hi ha...'.
Use 'hi ha' to mention existence, e.g., 'Hi ha molts parcs'.

title: Parlar de les aficions / Talking about hobbies
bridge: In Catalan, when talking about hobbies, the verb 'fer' (to do) is often used, similar to English. However, Catalan also uses the verb 'practicar' specifically for sports and activities, which is more precise than the general 'do' in English. Be careful with false friends like 'jogging' in English, which in Catalan is 'correr' (to run), not 'jogging'.
rule: To talk about hobbies in Catalan, use the structure 'M'agrada fer...' (I like to do...) or 'Pratico...' (I practice...). For sports, 'practicar' is more common. Use the present tense for habitual activities. Remember that Catalan adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun they modify, unlike English.

concept_examples.text: M'agrada fer fotos.
concept_examples.translation: I like to take photos.
concept_examples.phonetic: məˈɣaðə ˈfɛɾ ˈfɔtəs

concept_examples.text: Pratico futbol els caps de setmana.
concept_examples.translation: I play football on weekends.
concept_examples.phonetic: pɾəkˈtiko futˈβɔl əls ˈkaps də səˈtəˌmanə

concept_examples.text: Em sap fer manualitats a casa.
concept_examples.translation: I enjoy doing crafts at home.
concept_examples.phonetic: əm ˈsap ˈfɛɾ manu.ə.liˈtats ə ˈkazə

concept_examples.text: M'agrada llegir llibres de misteri.
concept_examples.translation: I like to read mystery books.
concept_examples.phonetic: məˈɣaðə ʎəˈɣiɾ ˈʎiβɾəs də misˈteɾi

common_error.explanation: English speakers often directly translate 'jogging' into Catalan, but the correct term is 'correr' (to run) or 'corrida' (jogging). 'Fer jogging' is not used in Catalan.

examples.note: Use 'm'agrada' for simple hobbies.
Use 'em sap fer' for enjoyable activities.
Use 'practicar' for sports.
Use 'jugar a' for team sports.
Use the infinitive form after 'm'agrada'.
Use 'fotografia' for the hobby of taking photos.
